thread: May 2026 FOI/EIR request — Great House Farm HER records (GGAT03586s, GGATE003872)
subject: Great House Farm, Williams/ Buckler Family, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan
note: Sent to several bodies by blind copy; Heneb's HER and heritage addresses were among them. The RCAHMW automatic acknowledgement in the same thread is catalogued on the RCAHMW page.
body:
Sir / Madam,

To all those whom it concerns, BCC'd into this email.

I write to request disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where applicable, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004.

This request concerns Great House Farm / Ty Mawr (Great House), Llandough, associated estate lands, historic occupation and related heritage records. My family is Buckler and before that Williams, and we occupied Great House Farm from 1667 until our forceful dispossession of it in 1988. Without our ownership ever having been estiguished and without BP ever having a ruling of ownership, only possession.

It's alledged our fee simple absolute and manorial title was stolen. And when BP registered our lands in their names in 1982, with our stolen title, my nan who challenged this all her life, during the 2 week land registry window to challenge BP's registration, which they achieved via purgergy and document/ identity fraud, she conveniently died. As my father did after his appeal of the 1987 mistake ruling was mistakely dismissed and his ECHR request blocked and home abruptly demolished, which he was prevented from stopping having been hospitalised and arrested without charges by armed force officers and possible SAS.

https://youtu.be/0eXOoj7eUCo?si=hcgSA2pFgEE943HG

I understand records may exist within the National Monuments Record of Wales, Historic Environment Record archives, archaeological consultations and planning files, including references already identified as:

• Great House Farm HER site entry – GGAT03586s
• Land at Great House Farm HER event entry – GGATE003872
• The 1990 archaeological assessment commissioned by BP Properties Ltd.

Please provide copies of, or access to:

1. All records concerning Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Great House Estate, Llandough including:

• surveys
• reports
• site notes
• photographs
• maps
• aerial imagery
• GIS layers
• archive material
• annotations
• title references
• occupancy references
• landscape records
• archaeological observations.

2. All internal and external correspondence involving:

• RCAHMW / NMRW
• Cadw
• GGAT / Heneb
• Vale of Glamorgan Council
• BP Properties Ltd
• developers
• planning authorities
• landowners, estate representatives or consultants.

3. Any documents discussing:

• estate ownership
• occupation history
• family occupation or association
• agricultural use
• commemorative tree planting or memorial planting
• estate boundaries
• title history
• acquisition history
• disputes concerning ownership, heritage status or land use
• estate restructuring, extinguishment, compulsory acquisition or title alteration.

4. Copies of all material linked to GGAT03586s and GGATE003872, including the archaeological assessment and associated correspondence.

5. Any records identifying historic occupants, proprietors, tenants or family associations, including references to the Williams family where present within archives.

6. Metadata identifying file creators, accession history, provenance, dates and retention schedules.

7. File indexes, archive references or schedules identifying further related material not already listed.

Please provide information electronically where possible.

If any material is withheld, please identify the exemption relied upon and provide the public interest assessment.

Regards,

Sion Buckler

5 [redacted]

thread: Sept 2026 EIR request — HER source file GGAT02038s (c.1880 ironwork)
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff
body:
HER Officer (Heneb: Glamorgan-Gwent),

This is a request for recorded information under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 and, so far as applicable, the Freedom of Information Act 2000, and under the public-access duty to the historic environment record.

I request the full HER source file for Great House Farm, Llandough (GGAT02038s and any linked event or find records), specifically:

1. The complete text of the entry or entries that refer to armour or medieval ironwork found under the rear wing / floor c.1880, including every source code and footnote.

2. A copy or transcript of the RCAHMW / Suggett 1988 material held on the HER file (GGAT’s 1990 assessment cites “RCAHMW 1988” for the museum attribution).

3. Any museum accession number, letter, or catalogue slip on the file that identifies where the ironwork went.

4. Any distinction on the file between:
(a) the c.1880 rear-wing ironwork;
(b) iron from the 1979 villa excavation south of the church;
(c) the 1994 cemetery iron girdle (Burial 631) later examined by the National Museum of Wales.

Please send electronic copies. I am an interested person researching the documented history of this site, not a commercial applicant.

Regards,

Sion Buckler
[redacted]

Dear Sir,

I write in response to your email, “Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff”, dated 8 September 2026.

I note that you have framed your request under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. The question of whether Heneb falls within the scope of those Regulations is a matter of legal determination, and nothing in this response should be taken as expressing a view on that matter. Irrespective of that question, access to the information concerned is not restricted and the information is available on request directly from the HER team. Following its digitisation, it is now freely available online via the Archwilio website via record 02038s.

The additional information referred to in your email dated 19 September 2026 will require further time to review, insofar as it is held within the HER. We will respond separately in relation to that information.

thread: Sept 2026 EIR request — HER source file GGAT02038s (c.1880 ironwork)
subject: RE: Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff
body:
HER Officer,

Great House Farm, Llandough — your letter of 6 October 2026, request of 8 September 2026 (GGAT02038s)

Thank you. I note that you point to Archwilio record 02038s and that you will reply separately on the 19 September 2026 email.

The 8 September request asked for the HER source file, not only the online summary. Archwilio 02038s does not supply:
1. the complete entry text on armour or medieval ironwork found under the rear wing or floor about 1880, with every source code;
2. a copy or transcript of the RCAHMW / Suggett 1988 material on the file;
3. any museum accession, letter, or catalogue slip naming where the ironwork went;
4. any recorded distinction between the c.1880 rear-wing ironwork, the 1979 villa iron south of the church, and the 1994 cemetery iron girdle (Burial 631).

Please give the record location before any viewing is discussed: series, accession, box, shelf, and catalogue id for the source file behind 02038s, and whether staff physically checked that the item is there (who, date, store). I am not requesting a screen-room viewing.

If any of the four items is not held, please name the systems searched and whether the physical source file was retrieved (EIR reg.5 and reg.9; reg.14 if you refuse).

Please also give a date for the separate reply on the 19 September email. The 8 September request was answered on day 20. An extension of the 19 September points should be notified if you need beyond 20 working days from 6 October.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
